The veteran has caught all seven of his targets this season for 48 yards, going OVER 10.5 in all three games. Montgomery isn’t going to get a ton of targets, but he’s caught multiple passes in each game thus far, with 19, 14, and 15 receiving yards. I expect him to keep that going against this Cowboys defense that allowed 40 receiving yards to Rachaad White two weeks ago.

highlights: Player Prop Countdown: Top 10 NFL Player Props for Week 4 We're now three weeks into the NFL season, which means we have a solid base of statistics and metrics to lean on when placing our bets. As I always do, I'm going to rank my top 10 player props for Week 4. Let's dive into them. Best NFL Week 4 Prop Bets 10) Ollie Gordon II UNDER 21.5 Rush Yards (-115) via Caesars With De'Von Achane now out for the season after suffering an ACL injury last week, fantasy owners and bettors alike were scrambling to get a piece of Ollie Gordon II. Unfortunately for those who did, the Dolphins' true No. 2 back, Jaylen Wright, is on his way to returning to the field this week. If that happens, Gordon's carries may be limited.

He and the rest of the Cardinals now get to face a Giants defense that ranks 27th in opponent dropback EPA and 23rd in opponent dropback success rate. That could lead to big things for the Arizona wide receiver. 4) Geno Smith OVER 21.5 Completions (+103) via Caesars Geno Smith has been impressive to start the season, despite the Jets being 1-2 through the first three weeks. results.title: Texans vs. Jaguars Best Prop Bets for NFL London Game in Week 6 (Bet on C.J. Stroud)
results.description: Breaking down the best prop bets for the AFC South matchup in London between the Houston Texans and Jacksonville Jaguars.
highlights: Here’s a breakdown of each of these prop picks – and their latest odds – for the London matchup in Week 6. Best NFL Prop Bets for Texans vs. Jaguars Odds via DraftKings Sportsbook Woody Marks OVER 14.5 Rush Attempts (-117) Brian Thomas Jr. UNDER 15.5 Receiving Yards (-111) C.J. Stroud OVER 251.5 Passing Yards (-113) Woody Marks OVER 14.5 Rush Attempts (-117) Texans running back David Montgomery is dealing with a groin injury, which should open up a massive role for Woody Marks in Week 6. Last week, Marks carried the ball 15 times for 62 yards in the win over Tennessee, playing well over 80 percent of Houston’s snaps. While the Texans have become a pass-first team in the 2026 season, Marks should monopolize touches in this backfield. Jacksonville is No. 1 in the league in EPA/Rush this season, so I prefer Marks’ attempts over any yardage number in this Week 6 matchup. Brian Thomas Jr.

An intriguing AFC South matchup begins Sunday’s Week 6 action in the NFL, as the Jacksonville Jaguars host the Houston Texans in London. This is the second straight London game for the Jags, as they pulled out a crazy victory against the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 5. That pushed Jacksonville to 4-1 this season, giving it a three-game cushion over Houston (who didn’t win until Week 5 against Tennessee) in the standings. Jacksonville is favored on Sunday, but bettors may not want to take a side in this game with Houston poised to make a run after a slow start. So, why not target some player props? I love betting on a few props in a standalone game, and there are some elite offensive weapons to consider in this matchup, including Houston’s Nico Collins and Jacksonville’s Parker Washington. I’ve narrowed things down to my three favorite props, as the Houston offense has been quietly solid throwing the ball while Jacksonville ranks sixth in the league in EPA/Play.

The Jaguars are top-10 defense in EPA/PAss this season, but they’ve allowed the third-most passing yards in the NFL. So, this is a pretty favorable matchup for C.J. Stroud, who ranks 14th in EPA/Play and 13th in success rate amongst quarterbacks with at least 50 plays this season. The former No. 2 overall pick has thrown for over 251.5 passing yards in four of his five games this season, and he has Nico Collins healthy in Week 6. Stroud is 3-for-3 hitting the OVER on this number when Collins plays, and the addition of Marvin Harrison Jr. could also improve this offense. Stroud also has attempted 31 or more passes in every game where he’s cleared this total. Since Jacksonville has been vulnerable to some big plays in the passing game, I love the OVER for Stroud in Week 6. Odds refresh periodically and are subject to change.
